name: Performance Lab Energy
summary: A caffeine-free 'cellular energy' capsule from Performance Lab: one 2-capsule serving gives 500mg acetyl-L-carnitine, 100mg R-lipoic acid, 100mg CoQ10, 10mg PQQ and 60mg magnesium, with every dose on the label. It is an energy supplement with a modest cognitive angle, not a nootropic stack, and none of its five actives reaches the reference dose in our dosing audit. Australian orders ship from the brand's Australian or UK depot (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05); it is sold direct to Australian buyers by the brand.
whatItIs: Performance Lab Energy is a caffeine-free capsule sold through performancelab.com. The vendor calls it a 'caffeine-free workout and daily energy supplement' for 'cellular energy, cardio performance, muscle strength, and clean focus'. One serving is 2 vegan pullulan capsules holding 500mg acetyl-L-carnitine (from acetyl-L-carnitine HCl), 100mg microencapsulated BioEnhanced R-lipoic acid, 100mg MicroActive Q10 (coenzyme Q10), 10mg BioPQQ (pyrroloquinoline quinone), 60mg magnesium as magnesium malate (14% of the US Daily Value) and 2.5mg BioPerine black pepper extract (95% piperine), which the vendor adds 'for enhanced absorption'; a bottle holds 30 servings. The label suggests 2 capsules in the morning or early afternoon on an empty stomach. The vendor states it is 'third-party tested for purity and potency' but names no lab. No entry was returned for 'Performance Lab Energy' or sponsor 'Performance Lab', 'Opti-Nutra' or 'Optinutra' when we searched the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG) and its cancellations-by-sponsor database on tga.gov.au on 2026-10-06, and the product page shows no AUST number; it is sold direct to Australian buyers by the brand.
howItWorks: Energy is built around mitochondria, the parts of cells that turn food into usable energy. Acetyl-L-carnitine carries fatty acids into mitochondria and donates acetyl groups for making acetylcholine; its positive cognitive trials used 1.5-3g a day in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, mild dementia or pre-frailty (Montgomery 2003 meta-analysis; Passeri 1990; Malaguarnera 2022), at least three times the 500mg here, and we found no trial in healthy young adults. PQQ improved some memory and attention scores in three small 12-week trials at about 20mg a day (Itoh 2016, Shiojima 2021, Tamakoshi 2023), two of them with authors affiliated with the PQQ manufacturer; Energy has 10mg. The vendor describes CoQ10 and R-lipoic acid as mitochondrial cofactors and antioxidants, but we found no positive cognitive trial of either: 300mg CoQ10 a day did not improve attention or working memory over 6 months in a trial in schizophrenia (Maguire 2021), and 100mg alpha-lipoic acid a day did not improve cognition in the only dose-matched trial we found, also in schizophrenia (De Lima 2023). BioPerine is there to aid absorption; we have not verified whether 2.5mg of piperine changes how well these ingredients are absorbed. Energy itself has not been tested in a published trial.
whatToExpect: Performance Lab says Energy starts working in around 30 minutes and that you may notice 'increased vitality', more motivation, a brighter mood and better muscle strength and cardio performance during exercise. It contains no caffeine or other stimulant. The positive cognitive trials of acetyl-L-carnitine and PQQ ran for 12 weeks or longer at 2 to 6 times these doses, so any cognitive effect at Energy's doses is uncertain. name: Performance Lab Omega-3
summary: A vegan omega-3 from Performance Lab: 3 softgels give 1,800mg algal oil (life's OMEGA 60) with 990mg total omega-3, including 540mg DHA and 270mg EPA, every amount on the label. The DHA dose sits below the 900mg-1.2g a day used in the positive memory trials, so it is a general-health omega-3 with a brain-health angle rather than a nootropic. Australian orders ship from the brand's Australian or UK depot (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05); it is sold direct to Australian buyers by the brand.
whatItIs: Performance Lab Omega-3 is an algae-based omega-3 supplement sold through performancelab.com. The vendor positions it 'to support optimal health and performance of the brain, eyes, heart and (much) more'. One serving is 3 NutriGels, softgels the vendor describes as vegan and free of gelatin and carrageenan (other ingredients listed: gellan gum, pectin, starch and glycerin), holding 1,800mg algal oil from life's OMEGA 60 with 990mg total omega-3 fatty acids, of which 540mg is DHA and 270mg is EPA; a bottle holds 30 servings. The label suggests 3 softgels with your first meal of the day. The vendor states it is 'third-party tested for purity and potency' and Clean Label Project certified; the product page shows the certification logo but no certificate or batch number. No entry was returned for 'Performance Lab Omega-3' or sponsor 'Performance Lab', 'Opti-Nutra' or 'Optinutra' when we searched the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG) and its cancellations-by-sponsor database on tga.gov.au on 2026-10-06, and the product page shows no AUST number; it is sold direct to Australian buyers by the brand.
howItWorks: DHA is the main structural omega-3 in brain cell membranes. In two 6-month trials it improved memory measures at 900mg a day in adults aged 55 and over with age-related cognitive decline (Yurko-Mauro 2010, sponsored by the algal-DHA maker Martek) and at 1.16g a day in healthy 18-45-year-olds with low DHA intake (Stonehouse 2013); this product supplies 540mg, below both. The wider evidence is mixed: a 2012 Cochrane review found no cognitive benefit from omega-3 supplements in cognitively healthy older adults. We found no trial of EPA alone for cognition; a 2024 dose-response meta-analysis of 24 trials of mixed EPA and DHA in adults aged 40 and over found an executive-function benefit trend above 500mg a day of total omega-3 (Suh 2024), which the 990mg here exceeds. The oil comes from algae rather than fish, so it suits vegans. Performance Lab Omega-3 itself has not been tested in a published trial.
whatToExpect: Performance Lab says Omega-3 starts working in around 30 minutes, that you may first notice improvements to hair, nails and skin, and that other benefits build over time; both positive DHA memory trials ran for 6 months, so do not expect a quick cognitive effect. Take 3 softgels with your first meal of the day. Our DHA ingredient page notes that in a 2021 meta-analysis of cardiovascular trials, omega-3 supplements were linked to a higher risk of atrial fibrillation, more so above 1g a day; one serving here gives 990mg of total omega-3, so ask your doctor first if you have a heart-rhythm condition or already take another omega-3. Orders to Australia ship from the brand's Australian depot in 3-6 working days or from its UK depot in 7-14 working days, depending on destination (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05). We saw only US-dollar prices ($49 one-time) when we checked.
